persons.name: Robert Allen Kinzie

occupation.note: 'The Kinzies, John and Robert A., merchants' in the 1833 roster. Andreas: he 'remained in Chicago when the rest of the family left in the spring of 1831, and early in 1832 erected a frame store on the West Side - the first frame store in Chicago - and probably the first frame building, aside from the one erected by Government for Billy Caldwell in 1828.'

persons.note: HE IS THE REASON CHARLES BUTLER AND ARTHUR BRONSON CAME WEST, which is the best-documented chain of causation in the whole 1833-35 record. Butler's letter of 1881: Bronson called on the New York Indian-goods merchant Daniel Jackson for information about Chicago, and Jackson 'said that he would then introduce him to a man from Chicago, who at that moment happened to be in his store making purchases of Indian goods. This was Robert A. Kinzie.' Kinzie offered them his quarter interest in the north fractional half of Section 10 - the ground Kinzie's Addition was laid out on. He was also a candidate at the first town election of 10 August 1833 and took nine votes, the highest of any unsuccessful candidate. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 — “Kinzie, R. A.” (poll_1833_018, line 39); Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Kinzie, Robert A.” (tax_1833_063, line 115). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Kinzie' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

resident_research.evidence_for: Published Cook County biography states Robert A. Kinzie remained mostly in Chicago from 1825 to 1840, built a frame store in 1832 and became a member of Kinzie, Davis & Hyde in 1835. Exact name, family context, business and year strongly corroborate the profile.

research_note: A MERCHANT WHOSE BUYING TRIP TO NEW YORK PUT THE TOWN ON THE MAP. This household is worth its place less for the man than for the mechanism it documents: in the winter of 1832-33 a Chicago trader buying Indian goods in a New York store is how eastern capital first heard that Chicago was worth buying. The population curve K1 is reconstructing starts there.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
